**Result:** Dq ≈ 815 cm⁻¹ (Δ ≈ 8 150 cm⁻¹), B ≈ 878 cm⁻¹ and C ≈ 3 980 cm⁻¹.

**Approach.** The three spin-allowed bands depend only on Dq and B. The spin-forbidden doublet band is the one that fixes C. I fitted them in two steps.

1. **Dq and B from the spin-allowed bands.** I fitted ⁴T₁→⁴T₂ (7 150), ⁴A₂ (15 200) and ⁴T₁(2) (19 200) with the d⁷ ligand-field matrices. This gives Dq ≈ 815 cm⁻¹ and B ≈ 878 cm⁻¹. The calculated bands are 7 086, 15 231 and 19 199 cm⁻¹, all within about 64 cm⁻¹ of the observed values. That gives B/B_free ≈ 0.90 if B_free ≈ 970 cm⁻¹ for Co²⁺, which I did not look up with the nephelauxetic tool.

2. **C from the doublet.** I held Dq = 815 and B = 878 fixed and scanned C. The energy of ²T₁(2), the second ²T₁ term, rises almost linearly with C at about 3 cm⁻¹ per cm⁻¹.
   - At C = 3 400 it lies at 19 392 cm⁻¹.
   - At C = 3 800 it lies at 20 592 cm⁻¹.
   - Setting it equal to 21 130 cm⁻¹ gives C ≈ 3 980 cm⁻¹, so C/B ≈ 4.5.

**Limits.** I did not refit all four bands together. Only the one doublet band constrains C, so C is less certain than Dq and B.

I first ran an automatic four-band fit. It kept C at its default of 4 499 and matched 21 130 cm⁻¹ to ⁴T₁(2) instead of ²T₁(2). That contradicts your assignment, so I did not use it.
